title: Quantum algorithms for general nonlinear dynamics based on the Carleman embedding: BQP-completeness of Poly-CNOP (printed as Theorem 7.6)
author: David Jennings, Kamil Korzekwa, Matteo Lostaglio, Andrew T Sornborger, Yi\u{g}it Suba\c{s}\dotlessi, Guoming Wang
work: Quantum algorithms for general nonlinear dynamics based on the Carleman embedding
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Theorem 7.6 (source0.tex lines 4113--4115), "Poly-CNOP is BQP-complete", the headline complexity result of the paper, delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 4117--4216 (100 lines, one adjacent proof environment, no gap and no deferral). The proof is a genuine two-sided complexity argument, not a routine verification. The hardness direction reduces the exponentially large linear oscillator problem Poly-CLOP, already known to be BQP-hard, to the nonlinear problem Poly-CNOP by setting the three nonlinear coefficient tensors to zero, which requires checking that the parameter, encoding and promise conditions of Poly-CNOP are all satisfied in that degenerate case. The containment direction is the substantive one: the author embeds the dynamics of the coupled nonlinear oscillators into a nonlinear Schroedinger equation through the substitution that turns the second-order oscillator system into a first-order evolution of an energy-normalised state, verifies that the embedded equation satisfies the hypotheses of the article's algorithm theorem for time-dependent quadratic nonlinearities, applies that algorithm, and then converts its output state into a decision about the ratio that Poly-CNOP asks about by estimating a projector expectation. The steps that carry the argument are the identification of the embedding and of its admissible parameters, the reduction of the decision to a state-preparation-and-measurement task with an explicit error budget, and the accounting of the oracle and gate resources; none of them is an unpacking of definitions. H3: a complete original research-paper proof of a main complexity theorem whose hypotheses are all retained.

primary.theorem: Theorem 7.6 (thm environment, statement: Poly-CNOP is BQP-complete)
